_comment: #117 — English is the source of truth. Every other locale file carries exactly this key set; the locale-parity test fails a build where they diverge, including one where a placeholder was dropped or invented. Keys are dotted and area-first (landing.*, settings.*) so a translator can work through one surface at a time. Placeholders are {name}, never {{name}} — the double-brace form is Bowire's own variable syntax and appears literally inside some strings.

tour.create-first-workspace.title: Create a workspace
tour.create-first-workspace.body:
A workspace is your project folder. It holds the URLs you discover, the environments + secrets you reference, and the collections / recordings / benchmarks you build.

Most operators name them after the project ("Petstore Staging", "Internal CMS").
tour.create-first-workspace.altLabel: You can also open the workspace chip in the topbar and pick "+ New workspace".
tour.ws-dialog-name.title: Name your workspace
tour.ws-dialog-name.body:
Type a name. Most operators name after the project ("Petstore Staging", "Internal CMS").

Click Next once you have a name.
tour.ws-dialog-template.title: Start from scratch or a template
tour.ws-dialog-template.body:
A template seeds the workspace with example URLs, environments, and collections so you can explore immediately. Try the REST or gRPC template — or stay on "Empty" to start clean.

Click Next once you pick.
tour.ws-dialog-submit.title: Create it
tour.ws-dialog-submit.body: Click Create. Bowire will set up the workspace, seed any chosen template, and switch the workbench to it.
tour.welcome.title: Welcome to Bowire
tour.welcome.body:
A multi-protocol API workbench — gRPC, REST, GraphQL, WebSocket, SSE, MQTT, all in one place.

This quick tour walks you from a blank workbench to your first response in five steps. You can skip anytime; we won't bring it up again.
tour.add-url.title: Step 2 — Point at your API
tour.add-url.body:
Open the Workspaces rail and add the URL of the API you want to call. Bowire works with any URL that exposes a discovery surface — OpenAPI / Swagger, gRPC reflection, GraphQL introspection — or a schema file you upload.

Good test URLs to try: petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json, countries.trevorblades.com.
tour.discover.title: Step 3 — Discover services
tour.discover.body:
Switch to the Discover rail. Once Bowire fetches your URL, it lists every service + method it found — grouped by protocol, searchable, filterable.

Click a method to open it in a new tab.
tour.execute.title: Step 4 — Send the request
tour.execute.body:
Once you have a method open, fill in the request form (or paste JSON) and hit Execute. Ctrl+Enter from anywhere in the request pane fires it too.

The response lands underneath — JSON, status, timing, headers — and the call is captured in your history so you can replay it later.
tour.wrap-up.title: You're set
tour.wrap-up.body:
That's the core loop: workspace → URL → discover → invoke. From here you can record a session and turn it into a mock, build collections, write tests, or wire envs + secrets.

Press F1 anywhere for in-app docs. Ctrl+/ shows every keyboard shortcut. Have fun.
tour.mock-intro.title: Build a mock from a recording
tour.mock-intro.body:
Mocks let you replay a captured session as a local HTTP server — handy for offline development, demos, or wiring an integration test against a frozen response set.

You need a recording first. If you don't have one yet, capture a few calls from Discover; the tour points you there.
tour.mock-go-recordings.title: Step 1 — Open the Recordings rail
tour.mock-go-recordings.body: Switch to the Recordings rail. If you already have a saved recording it shows in the sidebar; otherwise the empty card walks you through capturing one from Discover.
tour.mock-use-as-mock.title: Step 2 — Use as mock
tour.mock-use-as-mock.body: Pick a recording, then hit "Use as mock" in its detail toolbar. Bowire spins up a local MockServer on a free port and copies the URL to your clipboard.
tour.mock-switch-to-mocks.title: Step 3 — Inspect the running mock
tour.mock-switch-to-mocks.body:
The Intercept rail's "Mock servers" sub-tab lists every mock host you've started. Pick one to see its URL, copy it again, open the live request log, or stop the server.

Fire requests against the mock's port from your other tools and watch them stream in.
tour.mock-wrap-up.title: That's the mock loop
tour.mock-wrap-up.body: Recording → Use as mock → invoke against the mock port. From here you can chain it: benchmark the mock, share its URL with the team, or stop it from the Intercept rail's Mock servers sub-tab when you're done.
tour.env-intro.title: Set up environments
tour.env-intro.body: Environments scope variables, auth tokens, and secrets per deployment stage — staging vs. prod vs. local — so you can re-point an entire workspace at a different backend by toggling the active env.
tour.env-new.title: Step 1 — Create an environment
tour.env-new.body: Hit "+ New environment" on the workspace's envs overview. Give it a stage name like "staging" or "prod". The new env shows up in the workspace tree and in the topbar env dropdown.
tour.env-add-vars.title: Step 2 — Add variables
tour.env-add-vars.body:
Open the env editor (click the env name in the tree). Each row is a key=value pair — type a host, a token, a tenant id. Values are stored locally; mark a row as a secret to keep it out of exports.

You can paste a .env file in too — Bowire parses KEY=value lines.
tour.env-reference.title: Step 3 — Reference vars in a request
tour.env-reference.body: Anywhere a string field accepts input (URLs, headers, request body) you can write {{varName}} and Bowire substitutes the active env's value at send-time. Flip the active env from the topbar dropdown and the same request hits a different backend.
tour.env-wrap-up.title: You're set
tour.env-wrap-up.body: That's envs: create → add vars → reference. Use the topbar env dropdown to switch active env on the fly; the workspace tree shows the env count next to each workspace so you can see the spread at a glance.
tour.bench-intro.title: Benchmark a method
tour.bench-intro.body:
A benchmark repeats N calls at K concurrency and reports latency percentiles (p50 / p95 / p99) plus the status distribution.

Three shapes: single method (one unary call), collection (replay every item), or recording (replay every step). This tour walks the single-method shape.
tour.bench-go-rail.title: Step 1 — Open the Benchmarks rail
tour.bench-go-rail.body: Switch to Benchmarks. The sidebar lists saved specs; the main pane shows the configurator for the selected one.
tour.bench-new.title: Step 2 — New benchmark
tour.bench-new.body: Hit "New benchmark" on the empty card to create a fresh spec, then pick a method from the target dropdown. Or kick the tour off from Discover with the "Benchmark" button on any method.
tour.bench-configure.title: Step 3 — Set N + concurrency
tour.bench-configure.body:
Two knobs do most of the work: total iterations (N) and concurrent workers (VUs). Start small — 100 / 5 finishes in a few seconds and is enough to spot obvious regressions.

For sustained-load testing, switch the phase from iteration-bounded to duration-bounded (run for 60s @ 10 VUs) and read the steady-state RPS.
tour.bench-run.title: Step 4 — Run it
tour.bench-run.body:
Click Run. The progress bar ticks up as iterations land; cancellation is one click away if something's wrong.

When it finishes, the result panel below the configurator shows p50 / p95 / p99 latency, status-code distribution, and a sparkline of per-iteration durations. Re-run with tweaks; the last N runs stay in history so you can A/B them.
tour.bench-wrap-up.title: You're benchmarking
tour.bench-wrap-up.body: That's the loop: pick a target → set N + concurrency → run → read percentiles. Benchmark history sticks around per spec so you can see if today's change made things faster.
tour.rec-intro.title: Capture a recording
tour.rec-intro.body:
A recording is an ordered sequence of live calls Bowire captures while you drive the API. You can replay it later, spin it up as a mock host, or run it as a benchmark.

This tour walks the capture loop: arm → invoke → stop → save.
tour.rec-go-rail.title: Step 1 — Open the Recordings rail
tour.rec-go-rail.body: Switch to the Recordings rail. The sidebar lists saved recordings; the main pane shows the selected one or — when empty — the Start CTA you'll use next.
tour.rec-start.title: Step 2 — Start recording
tour.rec-start.body: Hit "Start recording" on the empty card. Bowire arms the capture pipeline and jumps you into Discover so the next thing you click can be recorded. A red dot in the topbar shows recording is live.
tour.rec-invoke.title: Step 3 — Invoke a few methods
tour.rec-invoke.body: From Discover, pick a method, fill the request, hit Execute. Each Execute is appended to the recording as one step. Chain a few calls together — that's your captured session.
tour.rec-wrap-up.title: Step 4 — Stop and reuse
tour.rec-wrap-up.body:
Click the red dot (or hit "Stop recording" on the Recordings rail) when you're done. The captured session lands in the sidebar with its steps.

From the detail toolbar you can rename it, replay it, "Use as mock" to spin up a fake host on the captured responses, or feed it to a benchmark.
tour.col-intro.title: Build a collection
tour.col-intro.body:
A collection is a folder of saved requests you can replay as a set — think Postman runner. Useful for smoke tests, demo scripts, or a personal "things I run every Monday" stash.

This tour walks the build loop: create → add requests → run.
tour.col-go-rail.title: Step 1 — Open Compose
tour.col-go-rail.body: The Compose rail hosts the canonical Collections + Presets surface (the standalone Collections rail was retired in v2.1). Switch to Compose; the side panel on the right lists every collection in the active workspace.
tour.col-new.title: Step 2 — New collection
tour.col-new.body:
Hit the + icon in the Library sidebar toolbar. A fresh, empty collection lands in the list with the focus on its name — type a label like "petstore-smoke" or "auth-flows".

Or import a Postman collection / OpenAPI spec via the Workspaces rail to seed one from existing material.
tour.col-add-items.title: Step 3 — Add requests
tour.col-add-items.body: Two ways to fill a collection: from Discover, right-click any method → "Save to collection"; or from Compose, the request builder's "Save" button lets you pick the target collection. Items show up in order in the detail pane.
tour.col-wrap-up.title: Step 4 — Run as a set
tour.col-wrap-up.body: When the collection has items, the detail pane's Run button replays them top-to-bottom and reports pass/fail per item. Hit it on every code change to catch regressions; export it as a .json to share with the team.
tour.flow-intro.title: Build a flow
tour.flow-intro.body: Flows chain API calls together: the response of one step becomes the input of the next. Use them for login → fetch → mutate sequences, smoke pipelines that need response-derived ids, or any "I always run these three in a row" workflow.
tour.flow-go-rail.title: Step 1 — Open the Flows rail
tour.flow-go-rail.body: Switch to the Flows rail. The sidebar lists saved flows; the canvas in the main pane is where you wire the nodes once a flow is selected.
tour.flow-new.title: Step 2 — New flow
tour.flow-new.body: Hit "New flow" on the empty card. The canvas opens with a single start node. From the node palette (left edge of the canvas) drag a Request node onto it — that's your first call.
tour.flow-chain.title: Step 3 — Chain steps
tour.flow-chain.body:
Add a second Request node and wire the start node's output into it. Inside the second request's URL or body, reference the first step's response with {{step1.response.body.<field>}}. Bowire substitutes the value at run-time.

Condition, Loop, Delay, and Variable nodes let you branch / iterate / wait / capture intermediate values.
tour.flow-wrap-up.title: Step 4 — Run + export
tour.flow-wrap-up.body: The Run button in the canvas header executes the flow top-to-bottom and shows per-step results. Export as .bwf to share, or "Export as collection" to lift the request nodes into a Collection that runs in CI.
tour.compose-intro.title: Compose a request
tour.compose-intro.body: Compose is the freeform request builder — type a URL, pick a method, fire. Useful when you don't want to (or can't) discover a schema first, when you're probing an unknown endpoint, or when you need a one-off call outside any collection.
tour.compose-go-rail.title: Step 1 — Open the Compose rail
tour.compose-go-rail.body: Switch to the Compose rail. Each request opens as its own tab in the strip across the top — Ctrl+L from anywhere opens a fresh one.
tour.compose-new.title: Step 2 — New request
tour.compose-new.body: Hit "New request" on the empty card. A fresh request tab opens with the cursor on the URL field. Type any URL — Bowire infers the protocol (REST / GraphQL / WebSocket / SSE / MQTT) from the scheme.
tour.compose-fill.title: Step 3 — Method + body
tour.compose-fill.body: Pick the HTTP method from the dropdown, switch to the Body tab if you need a payload (JSON / form / raw — Bowire renders the right editor). Headers, params, auth, env-variable references all sit in their own tabs alongside Body.
tour.compose-wrap-up.title: Step 4 — Execute
tour.compose-wrap-up.body: Hit Execute (Ctrl+Enter from anywhere in the request pane). The response lands below with status, timing, headers, and a syntax-highlighted body. Save the request into a Collection from the same toolbar for replay later.
tour.traffic-intro.title: Capture traffic
tour.traffic-intro.body: The Intercept rail's Captured sub-tab shows live HTTP flows intercepted by Bowire — every request that hits the host, with timing, status, request + response bodies. Useful when you're debugging a misbehaving client or learning how an app actually talks to its backend.
tour.traffic-go-rail.title: Step 1 — Open the Intercept rail
tour.traffic-go-rail.body: Switch to the Intercept rail. The Captured sub-tab streams flows in real time; the main pane shows the selected flow's request + response detail.
tour.traffic-source.title: Step 2 — Point a traffic source at Bowire
tour.traffic-source.body:
Two deployment shapes:

• Embedded — Bowire is mounted via MapBowire() in your ASP.NET host. Add app.UseBowireInterceptor() to the pipeline. Every request through that host shows up here.

• Standalone — run "bowire proxy" or "bowire interceptor" in a terminal as a sidecar and point your client at its URL. Bowire intercepts and forwards while capturing.
tour.traffic-invoke.title: Step 3 — Drive some traffic
tour.traffic-invoke.body: Hit the wired-up endpoint from your client (browser, curl, your app). Each flow lands in the sidebar as it happens — status code coloured by class (2xx green / 4xx amber / 5xx red), method + path on each row.
tour.traffic-wrap-up.title: Step 4 — Reuse the capture
tour.traffic-wrap-up.body: Pick a row to inspect the request + response in the main pane. "Send to recording" lifts the flow into a Bowire recording for replay / fuzzing; "Mock this route" generates a mock rule that intercepts the next matching call. The flows pane is a ring buffer — older entries roll off as new ones arrive.
tour.sec-intro.title: Scan for security risks
tour.sec-intro.body:
The Security rail runs threat-modelling over the API surface Bowire discovered: ranks endpoints by attack-surface risk, surfaces unauth'd mutations, mass-assignment shapes, weak auth signals.

Heuristic mode is on by default — sub-millisecond rules engine, no AI required. Flip the tier if you have an AI configured for semantic scoring on top.
tour.sec-need-endpoints.title: Step 1 — Get endpoints into Discover
tour.sec-need-endpoints.body: The threat-model reads from the same service tree Discover shows. You need at least one URL added (or a schema uploaded) so there are endpoints to rank. If Discover is empty, do that first — the empty-card on Security walks you there with "Open Discover".
tour.sec-go-rail.title: Step 2 — Open the Security rail
tour.sec-go-rail.body: Switch back to Security. With endpoints present, the threat-model surface shows the tier toggle (Heuristic / AI-assisted) and a Run button.
tour.sec-run.title: Step 3 — Run the scan
tour.sec-run.body: Pick a tier — start with Heuristic, it's instant and gives you a baseline. Hit Run. The endpoints get ranked by risk score with one-line rationale per row: "POST mutates state, no auth required", "DELETE on path with id parameter", &c.
tour.sec-wrap-up.title: You're scanning
tour.sec-wrap-up.body:
Click any ranked row to drill into the rule hits + remediation hint. Use the per-row "Generate test" button to spin up a security regression test against that endpoint.

The right-side Security drawer keeps the panel reachable from any rail so a scan-finding can stay open while you investigate in Discover or Compose.

settings.autoJsonDesc: Parse JSON payloads in WebSocket, MQTT, and SSE responses for pretty display
settings.identityCueDesc: Show a peripheral indicator in the active workspace’s colour.
settings.identityCueStyleDesc: Presentation used when the identity cue is on.
settings.alwaysInvokeUrlDesc: Expand the “Invocation URL” disclosure on every discovered method, instead of only when you open it. Handy when the API you call lives at a different host than its schema.
settings.watchIntervalDesc: Time to wait after one re-discovery finishes before starting the next. A discovery over every plugin takes seconds, so this is a gap, not a fixed cadence.
settings.mcpAdapterDesc: Expose Bowire’s discover / invoke / record primitives as MCP tools so AI agents (Claude, Cursor, Copilot) can drive the workbench.
settings.mcpForwarderDesc: Relay every incoming MCP tool call to a heavier Bowire on another host. Useful when an AI agent runs on a laptop but the schemas + recordings live on a build server.
settings.tourDesc: Replay the Getting-started tour that walks new operators through workspaces / Discover / Compose / Recordings.
settings.providerDesc: Backend that serves chat completions. Local (Ollama / LM Studio) keeps prompts on this machine; BYOK cloud (OpenAI / Anthropic / OpenRouter) calls the provider directly from this host; MCP routes through your existing MCP host.
settings.modelDesc: Model id served by the provider. Use 'ollama pull <name>' first; LM Studio uses the currently-loaded model. Empty falls back to the provider’s own default.
settings.autoDetectDesc: Probe 127.0.0.1:11434 (Ollama) and 127.0.0.1:1234 (LM Studio) on AI panel paint. Each probe times out at 300 ms. Off = fully offline, no local network calls.
settings.aiInvokeDesc: When on, the assistant can dispatch real calls via the bowire_invoke tool — every invocation is audited to ~/.bowire/.ai-actions.jsonl. Session-only: every workbench restart goes back to off.
settings.refreshDetectionDesc: Re-probe local providers and pull the current server-side configuration. Use this after starting Ollama / LM Studio.
settings.cat.pathDesc: Absolute or relative path to the JSON document. Leave blank to fall back to ~/.bowire/catalogue.json.
settings.cat.urlDesc: HTTPS endpoint returning the catalogue document shape ({ "version": 1, "entries": [...] }). Required.
settings.cat.authHeaderDesc: Sent verbatim as the Authorization request header (e.g. "Bearer eyJ..."). Leave blank to keep the existing stored value; clear to remove the stored value.
settings.cat.consulAddressDesc: Consul agent base URL — e.g. http://localhost:8500. Required.
settings.cat.aclTokenDesc: Optional X-Consul-Token sent on every catalogue request. Leave blank to keep the existing stored value.
settings.cat.datacenterDesc: When set, every catalogue API call is made with ?dc=<value>. Leave blank to let Consul pick the local DC.
settings.cat.tagFilterDesc: When set, only services carrying this tag are surfaced. Useful for scoping to env:staging or team:payments.
settings.cat.urlSchemeDesc: Consul does not carry the scheme intrinsically; pick http or https for the materialised service URLs.
settings.cat.k8sApiUrlDesc: Explicit Kubernetes API server URL (e.g. https://kubernetes.default.svc). Leave blank to auto-detect in-cluster env vars or kubeconfig.
settings.cat.k8sTokenDesc: Service-account / kubeconfig token. Leave blank to keep the existing stored value (or to fall back to in-cluster / kubeconfig auto-detection).
settings.cat.kubeconfigPathDesc: Path to a kubeconfig file. Leave blank to fall back to $KUBECONFIG / ~/.kube/config.
settings.cat.namespaceDesc: Namespace to query. Defaults to "default" outside a pod; the pod's own namespace when running in-cluster.
settings.cat.labelSelectorDesc: Standard k8s label selector — e.g. "bowire/discoverable=true". Forwarded verbatim as the labelSelector query param.
settings.cat.k8sUrlSchemeDesc: k8s Services don't carry the scheme intrinsically; pick http or https for the materialised service URLs.
settings.cat.caCertDesc: PEM-encoded CA bundle for the API server's TLS cert. Leave blank for the in-cluster CA / OS trust store.
settings.cat.skipTlsDesc: Local test clusters only (kind / k3d / minikube with self-signed certs). NEVER enable for production clusters.
settings.cat.hubUrlDesc: URL of the Bowire Agent hub (#128). The provider GETs {HubUrl}/hub/agents/catalogue on every refresh.
settings.cat.stubResponseDesc: JSON snapshot to feed the parser with instead of hitting the hub. Useful for validating the wire-shape contract before #128 ships.
settings.data.wsDeletionDesc: Soft moves the workspace to Trash so it can be restored within the retention window. Hard deletes immediately; Undo still works briefly via the action log, but the entry won’t be in the Trash.
settings.data.retentionDesc: How long soft-deleted workspaces (and other trashed entries) stay in the Trash before auto-purge. Ignored when deletion mode is Hard.
settings.data.resetAllDesc: Clear localStorage and reload — undo restores from a pre-reset snapshot
settings.data.clearRecordingsDesc: Move every recording in this workspace to the recordings trash
settings.data.clearCollectionsDesc: Move every collection in this workspace to the collections trash
settings.data.migrateVarsDesc: Rewrite legacy ${name} placeholders to the canonical {{name}} syntax (#145)
settings.data.runHistoryCapDesc: How many recent method-runs to keep in the per-workspace run-log. Older entries are FIFO-evicted. Powers the coverage chips on the Discover sidebar + the Run history view below.
settings.protoEnabledDesc: When disabled, this protocol’s services are hidden from the sidebar, chip suggestions, and the protocol switcher. The plugin stays loaded server-side so flipping it back on is instant.
rbAuth.clientSecretPublic: Client Secret (optional, public clients leave empty)
semantics.fuzzBadJson: Cannot fuzz: request body is not valid JSON. Edit the body, then retry.
landing.catalogueListsOne: lists {count} service this install can reach. Add the ones you need — no URLs to type.
landing.catalogueListsMany: lists {count} services this install can reach. Add the ones you need — no URLs to type.
landing.configureWorkspaceBody: A workspace is your project folder — URLs, environments, secrets, recordings all live in it. Open the workspace detail to add your first source.
landing.browseDiscoverBody: Already pointed Bowire at a service? Jump straight into Discover to pick a method and send your first request.
semantics.fuzzFieldMissing: Cannot fuzz: field {path} not found in the current request body. Right-click happened on a response field?
landing.tipPalette: Press Shift+/ to focus the command palette
landing.tipInvoke: Press Ctrl+Enter to invoke the selected method
landing.tipRepeat: Press R to repeat the last call
settings.autoWorkspaceForcedOn: Forced by the host (appsettings / CLI) — currently on.
settings.autoWorkspaceForcedOff: Forced by the host (appsettings / CLI) — currently off.
settings.autoWorkspaceEmbedded: On by default when Bowire is embedded: a first run seeds one workspace named after the host app and lands on Discover, where this host's own API is already listed. Turn it off to get the empty Home + Create-Workspace CTA instead. Takes effect after a reload of a fresh install.
settings.autoWorkspaceDesc: Seed a default "Personal" workspace on first run instead of showing the empty Home + Create-Workspace CTA. Takes effect after a reload of a fresh install.
compose.openInNewTab: {name} — click to open in a new tab
bench.pressRefresh: Press Refresh to load scheduled runs.
